Teaching or instruction; narrowly the five books of Moses, widely all Jewish teaching.

front: What do Jews mean by the chosen people?
back: A people given responsibility under the covenant to keep the Torah; not a claim of superiority.
The anointed one Jews expect to bring a time of peace and justice.
notes: Many Orthodox Jews expect a person from David's line; many Reform Jews speak of a messianic age.

notes: Views of the afterlife vary among Jews.

front: Who wrote the Thirteen Principles of Faith?
back: Moses Maimonides (Rambam), in the twelfth century CE.

front: Which two qualities of God do Jews hold together?
How do Orthodox and Reform Jews differ about the Torah?
back: Many Orthodox Jews: the whole Torah is from God and binding. Many Reform Jews: inspired by God and interpreted by each generation.
